flags.summary: Asked the price directly, the rep quoted a variable range of $2,000 to $8,000 with a midpoint of 'around like 5,000, 6,000' and said it depends, rather than the fixed $6,000 six-month figure quoted flatly to every other prospect in this batch.
evidence: The one-on-one coaching, it's quite a big range, but it's at least in the four figures.
And that range is usually between like 2,000 and 8,000. So there's a big range there, but it's at least in the four figures.
Yeah, so that's variable within those ranges. It depends a little bit. Usually it's around like the middle, so around like 5,000, 6,000.
So how do you guys go about pricing then?
Cross-reference, four other calls in this batch, same rep, same week: '6k for the six months', 'an investment of 6k USD', 'It's going to be 6k USD, which is 5.2k', 'everything is 6,000 USD in total.'

flags.summary: The rep tried to get the prospect to name his own budget before disclosing any price, and when the prospect declined, gave three successive non-answers to a direct pricing question.
evidence: I wanted to hear what you guys had to offer, and I wanted to hear the price
what is exactly the right fit, right? We have a few things that we could do. So what is sort of the range in which you're looking to invest in your own personal growth?

if the price isn't right, then I'm just not going to be wanting to go with you guys

evidence: I just finished medical residency, so I was just super stressed, couldn't really work out, and I had gotten sick previously. That was pretty long-standing sickness. Ended up getting better, fortunately.

I haven't worked out in basically like a year

evidence: I've done the calorie counting and everything, so I think I'll be successful with that, if that's the way you guys normally do things.
We don't do specific calorie counting. We don't do only chicken and rice.
